author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty through the address
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory, the paged page and the machine-readable list, accept an optional specialty in the address and list only veterinarians holding it. The match is on the whole name, ignoring case. The filter has no page control.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-003] GET /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only veterinarians holding that specialty, paginated over the narrowed list (page count and totals reflect the narrowed list).
[REQ-VET-003] On a narrowed /vets.html spanning more than one page, every pagination link carries the same specialty parameter.
[REQ-VET-003] GET /vets?specialty=<name> returns only veterinarians holding that specialty in the existing machine-readable document shape.
[REQ-VET-003] Matching ignores letter case: specialty=RADIOLOGY matches radiology on both surfaces.
[REQ-VET-003] Matching is on the whole name, not a prefix: specialty=radio matches no veterinarian on both surfaces.
[REQ-VET-003] A specialty no veterinarian holds (including a name that is no specialty) returns HTTP 200 with the normal page or document and an empty veterinarian list.
[REQ-VET-003] An empty or whitespace-only specialty value behaves exactly as if the parameter were absent, on both surfaces.
[REQ-VET-003] A veterinarian listed in a narrowed result still shows every specialty they hold (PRD edge case 2).
[REQ-VET-001, REQ-VET-004] Without the parameter both surfaces behave as today: /vets.html pages over every veterinarian, /vets returns every veterinarian unpaged.
non_goals: No form, dropdown, or other page control for the filter on either surface (owner decision, intake line 1); a visible control may come as a follow-up request.
No free-text, name, or prefix search for veterinarians (NG-9, narrowed).
No pagination added to the machine-readable /vets list.
No narrowing to veterinarians holding no specialty, and no more than one specialty per request.
No trimming rule for a padded non-blank value: whether ' radiology ' matches is an open PRD question; do not test it either way.
No on-page indication of the active filter.
REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the vet feature package, following the existing repository-plus-paging pattern (system-design § Contracts: VetRepository, VetController). It adds two pieces of new ground, both recorded as ADRs. First, case-insensitive matching is written in the query, never left to the vendor schema. Second, reads keyed by a caller-supplied value stay out of the unbounded vets cache. The REQ-VET-004 reinstatement made the Overview's 'no JSON API' line and the Known Defects row 'machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement' stale; both are fixed. Contracts rows now carry REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004. A new § Scale and Load records the directory rows. Grounding is grep-based, a weaker basis than the IDE oracle, which is not connected: VetRepository has only the two @Cacheable("vets") findAll methods, the H2 and PostgreSQL specialties.name columns compare case-sensitively, and MySQL's default collation does not.
integration_points: Binding, GET /vets.html: request-scoped scalars only, the existing int page plus an optional String specialty @RequestParam. No persisted type is bound.
Binding, GET /vets: one optional String specialty @RequestParam. No persisted type is bound.

Normalization: VetController maps a null, empty, or whitespace-only specialty to absent and then calls the existing cached findAll methods unchanged. This is binding, not a business rule (architecture-principles § Pattern catalog, Web controller row). A non-blank value is passed through untrimmed; the trimming rule is an open PRD question and stays untested.

VetRepository gains two uncached read methods, a paged one and an unpaged one, narrowed to a specialty name. Both are explicit parameterized JPQL: select v from Vet v where exists (select s from v.specialties s where lower(s.name) = lower(:specialty)). Use no join-fetch and no WHERE on a joined alias, because either filters the eager specialty collection down to the matched one (PRD edge case 2). The exists form also keeps Spring Data's derived count query correct for page totals. No LIKE (ADR 2026-10-25-vendor-portable-case-insensitive-matching).

vetList.html: every pagination link (numbered, first, previous, next, last) carries specialty when it is present, built with Thymeleaf link-expression parameters, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}. A null parameter is then omitted and the value is URL-encoded. Do not concatenate the value into a URL string. The controller exposes the normalized specialty as a model attribute.

Double, repository boundary (matching semantics: case, whole name, every held specialty, narrowed page totals): the real H2 database, in a @DataJpaTest beside ClinicServiceTests' vet tests. The seed data already holds multi-specialty veterinarians. A stub cannot exercise the query, so these assertions must not live only in VetControllerTests.

Double, framework transport (VetControllerTests): MockMvc, the sanctioned mock. Its existing @MockitoBean VetRepository stub is tolerated for routing, normalization, model-attribute, and pagination-link assertions. The reason: a @WebMvcTest slice loads no JPA, and a hand-written double would re-implement the query semantics under test. New tests may reuse that stub but must not assert matching semantics through it.

Double, vendor boundary: PostgreSQL is the case-sensitive vendor, so a case-differing specialty match is worth one assertion in PostgresIntegrationTests (Testcontainers, disabled without Docker). It is optional for the gate, which runs on H2.

findings.description: The conditional `${specialty != null} ? @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})} : @{/vets.html(page=...)}` is repeated verbatim across five sibling pagination links (numbered, first, previous, next, last). A future reader must keep five copies in step, and the reason for the branch (Thymeleaf renders a null link parameter as `&specialty=`) is stated nowhere in the template.
findings.fix: Compute the filtered-or-unfiltered decision once (th:with on the pagination container, or a fragment taking the page number) and reference it from each link. Keep the explicit `!= null` test.
